concepts.name: NDA effective date
justifications: The agreement expressly defines the Effective Date as 1 February 2027, distinct from its signing on 29 January 2027.

concepts.name: NDA permitted purpose
predicted: evaluating a possible minority investment by the recipient in the discloser's marine sensor business under project glassfinch.
gold: evaluating a possible minority investment by the recipient in the discloser's marine sensor business under project glassfinch.
values: Evaluating a possible minority investment by the Recipient in the Discloser's marine sensor business under Project Glassfinch.
justifications: The agreement expressly defines this as the sole Permitted Purpose.

concepts.name: NDA disclosure window end
justifications: The effective termination notice closes the disclosure window on 30 November 2027, earlier than its ordinary end date. The return request does not itself terminate the window.

concepts.name: NDA contractual forum
justifications: The agreement designates the courts of Oslo as the parties’ contractual forum.

concepts.name: NDA signatory entities
justifications: FjordSignal AS is identified as registered in Norway and as the Discloser.
Talus Ventures AB is identified as registered in Sweden and as the Recipient.

concepts.name: Protected assets at the April snapshot
justifications: At the snapshot, LUMEN's non-public combination, SHORE's complete package despite its previously known component, CEDAR before its later public release, and BASALT despite breach-caused posting remain protected. ORACLE's late confirmation had not yet been accepted, and MICA was independently developed before disclosure.

concepts.name: ORACLE timely confirmation deadline
justifications: Counting five Business Days after the Thursday 25 March 2027 disclosure, with 26 and 29 March excluded, the fifth Business Day is 5 April 2027.

concepts.name: ORACLE protection timeline
predicted: protection was not continuous. oracle was provisionally protected from its oral disclosure on 25 march 2027 at 14:00 until the five-business-day confirmation deadline, 5 april 2027 at 17:00 utc. although the confirmation was sent on 5 april at 16:58, it was not delivered to the designated mailbox until 6 april at 09:05, so it was late; sending did not meet the deadline. the provisional protection therefore ended at the deadline, creating a gap until the recipient's written acceptance on 8 april at 10:00, which restored protection prospectively only.
gold: oracle is provisionally protected from the 25 march oral disclosure until 5 april 2027 at 17:00 utc. confirmation sent before that deadline arrived late on 6 april at 09:05, so protection lapses after the deadline. it resumes prospectively when the recipient expressly accepts on 8 april at 10:00 utc; the gap is not cured retroactively.
values: Protection was not continuous. ORACLE was provisionally protected from its oral disclosure on 25 March 2027 at 14:00 until the five-Business-Day confirmation deadline, 5 April 2027 at 17:00 UTC. Although the confirmation was sent on 5 April at 16:58, it was not delivered to the designated mailbox until 6 April at 09:05, so it was late; sending did not meet the deadline. The provisional protection therefore ended at the deadline, creating a gap until the Recipient's written acceptance on 8 April at 10:00, which restored protection prospectively only.
justifications: The confirmation deadline is measured in Business Days and expires at 17:00 UTC on the final day. Delivery occurs upon arrival at the designated mailbox, not when sent; late confirmation alone does not restore protection, while written acceptance restores it only prospectively.

concepts.name: Entire SHORE package excluded by prior possession
justifications: Prior possession is established only for the smaller module, not the complete package. The package also contains new, non-public content and no evidence establishes prior possession of the complete combination.

concepts.name: CEDAR end of protection
justifications: The entire schedule was independently and lawfully released to the unrestricted public on this date, establishing the public-information exclusion. That exclusion ends protection as soon as established, despite the ordinary duration that would otherwise apply.

concepts.name: People permitted LUMEN access at the September snapshot
justifications: Elin meets the employee, undertaking, security-check, and named-approval requirements. Marek’s employer qualifies as an Affiliate because the Recipient controls 52% of its votes at the snapshot, and all his required protections and approvals are effective by then; Oskar qualifies as a professional adviser with an enforceable duty of confidence, completed security check, and effective named approval. No stated competitor bar applies to these people.

concepts.name: Talus Research qualifying voting percentage
justifications: At the access snapshot, the Recipient directly holds votes representing 48% and has an irrevocable proxy over a disjoint 4% that is effective on that date. Both count toward voting power, for a total of 52%.

concepts.name: Marek earliest authorised LUMEN access
justifications: On this date, the currently effective 48% direct votes plus the 4% irrevocable proxy make Talus Research an eligible Affiliate. Marek’s undertaking and security check were already effective, and his named clean-room approval takes effect on 14 September, so this is the first date all stated access conditions are met.

concepts.name: Executed competitor consent date for Pia
Q-27 notice deadline date
justifications: Because notice was initially prohibited, the deadline was the earlier of six continuous hours after the prohibition was lifted (17:20 on 5 July) and the production time. The six-hour deadline came first.

concepts.name: Q-27 notice lateness in minutes
justifications: The prohibition was lifted at 11:20, making the applicable deadline six continuous hours later, 17:20, which is earlier than the production time. The notice actually arrived at 17:55, so it was 35 minutes late.

concepts.name: Q-27 permitted production units
justifications: The final binding narrowing order requires all of P1 and only non-privileged subsection P3A. P2 and P4 were withdrawn, and P3B was determined privileged and outside the production duty.

concepts.name: WORK-1 deletion deadline
justifications: The return request was delivered on 22 November, the earlier trigger. Counting ten Business Days after that date, excluding the specified holidays and weekends, gives 8 December; WORK-1 remains subject to this deadline despite being restored on 1 December, and no binding preservation order covers it.

concepts.name: BK-1 deletion deadline
justifications: The Section 7.1 trigger is the earlier return request delivery on 22 November, and the 45-calendar-day limit runs from the following day. BK-1’s scheduled overwrite on 30 December is earlier than that limit, so it is the latest permitted deletion date; restoring a copy does not restart either clock.

concepts.name: Artifacts permitted retention at the December snapshot
justifications: The segregated counsel-held archive, immutable backup before its scheduled overwrite, and exact copies covered by the still-binding preservation order qualify for the specified retention exceptions at the snapshot. WORK-1 is an ordinary active copy, and NOTE-1 is not covered by an exception.

concepts.name: NOTE-1 model training permitted as residual knowledge
justifications: Training a model on Confidential Information or derivatives that reveal it is prohibited without a separate signed licence. NOTE-1 contains deliberately recorded notes and quantitative parameters, which are excluded from residual-knowledge permission, and retention exceptions do not authorize training.
